sources.claim: MLPerf LLM server benchmark latency limits: time-to-first-token <= 2 s and time-per-output-token <= 200 ms - so a few ms of added fiber RTT from a remote Texas site is <1% of the TTFT budget.

sources.quote: the balance of Winter ’26/’27 (December through March) eased 1.8 cents to -$1.15, Summer ’27 improved 3.6 cents to -$1.57, and Winter ’27/’28 firmed 2.6 cents to -$2.08. Spring 2028, still the weakest part of the curve, held near -$2.41.
sources.claim: Waha forward basis (early Nov 2026): about -$1.15 winter 26/27, -$1.57 summer 27, -$2.08 winter 27/28, -$2.41/MMBtu spring 2028 vs Henry Hub.

sources.quote: The next period with the greatest risk of renewed constraints appears to be early 2028, before another wave of pipeline capacity is scheduled to come online.
sources.claim: AEGIS: Permian egress risk returns in early 2028 before the next pipeline wave (Eiger Express mid-2028) - negative Waha could recur.

sources.quote: Energy Transfer also placed its 275 MMcf/d Mustang Draw II processing plant in the Midland Basin into service in October
sources.claim: Typical new Permian processing plant = 275 MMcf/d (ET Mustang Draw II, Oct 2026); a 1 MW recip block needs only ~0.2-0.25 MMcf/d, <0.1% of plant residue output.

sources.quote: The supply or delivery of natural gas cannot be curtailed under a firm contract except under unforeseeable circumstances.
sources.claim: EIA: firm gas contracts cannot be curtailed except for unforeseeable circumstances, whereas interruptible contracts can be cut when firm holders use capacity or others outbid; a wellhead flare-gas deal is effectively interruptible.

sources.quote: These long-term contracts will provide behind-the-meter power to support Targa’s continued investment in natural gas processing infrastructure in the Permian Basin, with full deployment expected in early 2028.
sources.claim: ProPetro PROPWR contracted ~230 MW of Permian behind-the-meter gas power for Targa processing (Sept 2026; total ~510 MW contracted), full deployment early 2028 - Permian BTM power competes for the same engines.

sources.quote: EPA described circumstances involving gathering-system pressure, maintenance, production surges and insufficient pipeline capacity.
sources.claim: EPA's Apr 30, 2026 memo recognizes Permian gathering-system pressure, maintenance and takeaway limits interrupt associated-gas offtake - i.e. gathering-line supply also has outages a BTM site must ride through.

sources.quote: Developers can expect average greenfield costs of $17.6 million per MW for the most modern facilities
sources.claim: Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Development Cost Guide: average all-in greenfield DC cost $17.6M per MW (excludes IT/GPUs; includes land, shell, MEP, power), up 21% vs late-2024.

sources.quote: Installed recip-engine plants vary most, from $1,292/kW to $4,149/kW.
sources.claim: Hyper Tech Research (158 public data points, 2023-2026): installed recip-engine BTM plants range $1,292-4,149/kW.

sources.quote: $1,000–1,200 per kW for a delivered 10–50 MW generation package, 2026 $1,450–1,650 per kW with balance of plant
sources.claim: 2026 BTM gas generation: delivered 10-50 MW package $1,000-1,200/kW; $1,450-1,650/kW with balance of plant (before full installation ~+$900/kW).

DOE CHP fact sheet DOE/EE-2764 (2020$, CHP scope incl. heat recovery): installed recip cost $3,150/kW at 500 kW, $2,800/kW at 1 MW, $2,550/kW at 2 MW, $2,000/kW at 4.5 MW - strong diseconomies below ~5 MW.
DOE CHP fact sheet DOE/EE-2841 (2020$): small simple-cycle gas turbine installed cost $5,200/kW at 2 MW, $3,400/kW at 5 MW, $2,500/kW at 10 MW - turbines are uneconomic at 0.5-5 MW vs recips.

sources.quote: 5.45 for fuel, less 1.75 for the thermal credit, plus 1.90 for maintenance, giving 5.6 cents to generate
sources.claim: DOE CHP screening example: recip maintenance 1.90 c/kWh (~$19/MWh) alongside 5.45 c/kWh fuel.

sources.quote: fuel rises from 7,474 Btu/ekW-hr at 100% load to 7,668 at 75% and 8,526 at 50%: 8,526 ÷ 7,474 = 1.14, or 14% more fuel per kWh at half load.
sources.claim: Recip part-load penalty: heat rate rises 7,474 -> 8,526 Btu/ekWh from 100% to 50% load (+14% fuel per kWh) - N+1 sizing that runs engines at ~50-75% costs fuel.

sources.quote: Combustion turbine 841 Internal combustion engine 1,490
sources.claim: EIA (released Jul 2026): capacity-weighted construction cost of generators installed in 2024 - internal combustion engines $1,490/kW, combustion turbines $841/kW (utility-scale; battery storage $1,469/kW).

sources.quote: the minimum separation distance from the engine housing is 5 ft to any opening in an adjacent building and 5 ft to any structure with combustible walls, building openings, overhangs, and vegetation.
sources.claim: NFPA 37 outdoor engines: 5 ft minimum from engine housing to building openings and to combustible-wall structures/vegetation (reducible with 1-h rated walls or listed enclosures) - genset-to-container spacing floor.

sources.quote: ESS located outdoors shall be separated by a minimum of 10 feet (3048 mm) from the following exposures: Lot lines . Public ways . Buildings.
sources.claim: IFC 2024 1207.8.3 (based on NFPA 855-2023): outdoor BESS >= 10 ft from lot lines, public ways, buildings and other exposures; reducible to 3 ft with 1-h barrier or UL 9540A-backed enclosure.

sources.quote: remote outdoor installations include ESS located more than 100 feet (30 480 mm) from buildings, lot lines , public ways , stored combustible materials, hazardous materials, high-piled stock and other exposure hazards.
sources.claim: IFC 2024 1207.8.1: BESS >100 ft from buildings, lot lines and hazards qualifies as 'remote' with relaxed requirements - on a large rural pad, a 100 ft setback simplifies BESS compliance.

sources.quote: a noise is presumed to be unreasonable if the noise exceeds a decibel level of 85 after the person making the noise receives notice from a magistrate or peace officer that the noise is a public nuisance.
sources.claim: Texas Penal Code 42.01: noise presumed unreasonable above 85 dB (after notice) - the only statewide noise yardstick in unincorporated Texas counties absent local rules.

sources.quote: The noise level of the silent unit is 72dB(A)/7m
sources.claim: Vendor (EN Energy) 1 MW silent containerized gas genset: 72 dB(A) at 7 m - by distance attenuation ~50 dB(A) at ~90 m, far below the Texas 85 dB nuisance presumption.

sources.quote: Electrical Efficiency up to 42.5 % Thermal Efficiency up to 47.7 % L: 12,200 x W: 3,000 x H: 2,700 - 5,300 mm
sources.claim: Jenbacher J420 (~1.5 MW, 60 Hz variant) package footprint 12.2 x 3.0 m (40-ft container class, ~37 m2 or ~400 sq ft per 1.5 MW before clearances) - one engine ~= one AI Block's IT load.

sources.quote: with an initial buildout expected to deliver 8 megawatts of modular data center capacity and a target commercial operation date in the first quarter of 2027.
sources.claim: Energy Vault Snyder AI (Permian edge, Scurry County TX): 8 MW of Crusoe Spark modular DCs (10 units, ~0.8 MW each) started Jul 2026, COD Q1 2027 (~8 months), expandable to 25 MW.

sources.quote: Crusoe will lease the units back from Energy Vault as “powered shell” infrastructure
sources.claim: Commercial model precedent: Energy Vault owns Crusoe Spark units and power, leasing them back to Crusoe as 'powered shell' - matches the AI Block 'sell power, cooling, space' model.
